recent_articles.title: Indian Army, IAF contain major forest fire in Himachal’s Kasauli slopes - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Indian Army**, in collaboration with the **Indian Air Force** and local authorities, successfully contained a major forest fire that broke out on Tuesday (May 26, 2026) in Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh.  Army troops conducted ground firefighting efforts supported by water carriers and fire tenders, while IAF helicopters performed aerial "Bambi Bucket" operations to draw water from Sukna Lake. The combined effort significantly contained the blaze and prevented its spread into vulnerable forest zones. All personnel involved remain safe, with no reported casualties among civilians or responders.

recent_articles.title: Indian Army, IAF contain major forest fire in Himachal’s Kasauli slopes - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Indian Army**, in collaboration with the **Indian Air Force** and local civil authorities, successfully contained a major forest fire that erupted in the Gilbert Trail and Upper Mall area of Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh. The fire broke out on Tuesday afternoon and prompted an immediate response from the **Kasauli Brigade** to prevent its spread through challenging terrain.

recent_articles.title: Row over Sabeer Bhatia saying India should ‘appreciate every chapter of its history’, Sridhar Vembu responds - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sabeer Bhatia**, Indian-American co-founder of Hotmail, sparked a debate on social media by urging Indians to acknowledge both positive and negative aspects of their history. **Sridhar Vembu**, billionaire co-founder of Zoho Corporation, responded by comparing Bhatia's remarks to asking Jews to "appreciate" the Holocaust.  Vembu argued that painful periods of history should not be simply "appreciated," citing the role of remembering past suffering in building a strong future. The online disagreement highlights differing perspectives on India's historical narrative and its impact on national identity.

recent_articles.title: Fuel shortage hits pumps amid panic buying; OMCs call for calm, say supply is steady - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Farmers** across several states in India are facing fuel shortages due to the recent hike in fuel prices.  The **Centre** has implemented price hikes to mitigate losses for its oil marketing companies (OMCs), but this has led to supply disruptions and long queues at petrol stations.  In Maharashtra, **farmers** are struggling to procure diesel for their tractors, while in Punjab, the **Punjab Petrol Pump Dealers Association** reports short supplies of both petrol and diesel. The situation is impacting agricultural activities and transportation, with some fuel stations even running dry.  The **Petroleum Ministry** has assured the public that there is no shortage of fuel but urged people to avoid panic buying.

recent_articles.title: Scorching days, restless nights: Heatwave tightens grip across parts of India - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** experienced scorching temperatures exceeding 44° Celsius in several regions, prompting **hospitals** in Punjab to activate heat stroke management units. The **IMD** issued heatwave alerts for three districts of Jharkhand and warned of rising temperatures across Delhi, Haryana, and Chandigarh.  Veterinarians and animal rescuers reported an increase in distressed birds and animals suffering from dehydration and heatstroke. In Himachal Pradesh, a yellow warning for heatwave conditions was issued for parts of the state. **Chief Ministers** of various states ordered officials to ensure adequate drinking water availability, while **Congress leader Kishori Lal Sharma** raised concerns about power supply disruptions in Uttar Pradesh's Amethi constituency.

recent_articles.title: 806 locals held, 97 properties attached, 41 demolished in anti-drug drive in J&K in 30 days: DGP Nalin Prabhat - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **J&K Police** conducted a major anti-drug campaign between April 11 and May 13, resulting in the arrest of 806 individuals under the NDPS Act, the attachment of 97 properties worth ₹41.85 crore, and the demolition of 41 properties linked to drug trafficking. **Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat** stated that these actions were part of a broader effort to dismantle drug networks operating across states and combat Pakistan-sponsored terrorism and narco-terrorism.  The campaign also saw the cancellation or suspension of driving licenses for 162 individuals involved in narcotics activities, the revocation of registration certificates for 92, and the impounding of 10 passports.

recent_articles.title: School education index: Kerala betters grade, score - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Despite the denial of funds by the **Union government**, **Kerala** has improved its performance in the **Union Ministry of Education’s Performance Grading Index 2.0 for States/Union Territories (UT) for the year 2024-25**. The state received a Prachesta-2 grade, an improvement from Prachesta-3 in 2023-24, with scores rising from 594.2 to 687.7.  **Kerala** achieved the topmost Utkarsh grade (72.8-80) in access and the Uttam-1 grade (81-90.9) in teacher education and training, among other achievements. The report highlights Kerala's progress despite challenges, including a lack of funding from the **Union government**.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: AAP holds protests against BJP over ED action against Punjab Minister Sanjeev Arora - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)** held protests across Punjab against the **BJP** following the ED's arrest of Punjab Industries Minister Sanjeev Arora on charges of GST fraud. The protests, led by AAP leaders including Hardip Singh Mundian and Mohinder Bhagat, escalated into clashes with BJP workers in Ludhiana and Bathinda.  The **BJP** accused AAP workers of attacking their activists while the **AAP** condemned the police's alleged inaction.

recent_articles.title: ED raids Punjab Minister Sanjeev Arora, linked persons again - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Directorate of Enforcement (ED)** conducted fresh searches on Saturday, May 9, 2026, targeting **Punjab Industries Minister Sanjeev Arora** and others allegedly connected to him. The raids focused on **Mr. Arora's** official residence in Chandigarh and a real estate company in Gurugram, Haryana. This action was taken under the criminal sections of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) following previous raids in April that were conducted under civil provisions of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).

recent_articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lalit Jain**, Director of Census Operations (DCO), **Haryana**, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

recent_articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haryana** administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  **Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar** stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. **Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan** flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

recent_articles.title: BJP’s Bengal sweep fires up Punjab unit; AAP moves to deflate buzz - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP**'s strong performance in West Bengal, Assam, and Puducherry has fueled hopes for a similar outcome in Punjab, where elections are scheduled soon.  The **Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)** responded by asserting that the BJP's prospects in Punjab are bleak.  **Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann** criticized the BJP's track record in Punjab, highlighting past injustices and farm law protests as evidence of their unpardonable sins.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Around 82 lakh households have opted for self enumeration as field visits begin in 5 states - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union government** announced that over 82 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the initial Houselisting and Housing Operations (HLO) phase of Census 2027. The exercise, which commenced on May 1st in several states including Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan, aims to collect data about household facilities and demographics.  The HLO will continue until May 30th, with trained enumerators visiting each house for verification.

recent_articles.title: High drama in Punjab Assembly; Congress, Akali Dal allege CM Mann was drunk during House proceedings - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Opposition parties in Punjab, including the Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal, have accused **Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann** of appearing intoxicated during a session of the Vidhan Sabha.  They demanded an alcohol test and called for dope testing of all MLAs.  Congress leader Sukhpal Singh Khaira urged **Arvind Kejriwal**, the national convener of the Aam Aadmi Party, to take action against **Mann**. Rajya Sabha MP Swati Maliwal also accused **Mann** of being intoxicated at public events and demanded an alcohol test. The Congress Legislative Party has formally written to the Speaker requesting immediate alco-meter and dope testing of all members.  Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema refuted the allegations, calling them false and baseless.

recent_articles.title: NGT issues notice to Centre over risks from hanging glaciers in central Himalaya - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** has ordered responses from various government agencies and organizations regarding the dangers posed by hanging glaciers in central Himalaya. The tribunal, hearing a case based on a newspaper report, found that four researchers from different institutions assessed the potential impact of glacier retreat and instability, concluding that ice avalanches could reach major settlements.  The NGT also noted violations of the Environment (Protection) Act related to these concerns, prompting the inclusion of several government bodies as respondents in the proceedings.

recent_articles.title: 26 candidates bag perfect 100 NTA score in JEE-Main - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **NTA** announced that 26 candidates achieved a perfect score of 100 on the JEE-Main entrance exam, surpassing last year's total.  Over 13 lakh candidates took the exam in two sessions, with more than eight lakh appearing in both. The scores are normalized across shifts and range from 100 to 0 for each shift. The candidates, all males, hail from various states including Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Rajasthan, Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, and Gujarat.

recent_articles.title: PCR tests for amoebic fever now at Kozhikode MCH’s microbiology lab - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Government Medical College Hospital** in Kozhikode has equipped its microbiology lab with facilities to conduct PCR tests for the identification of Naegleria fowleri, Acanthamoeba spp., and Balamuthia mandrillaris. This allows for species identification and confirmation of amoebic meningoencephalitis directly at the hospital, eliminating the need for sending samples to other labs.  The lab has already tested a majority of samples for Acanthamoeba spp., with 83 cases of amoebic meningoencephalitis and 15 deaths reported in the state this year.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 9 States and 3 UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by **West Bengal**, with a net deletion of 83.86 lakh. The SIR phase II identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters across these states and UTs.  The consolidated electoral rolls saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 12 States and UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which saw a significant reduction in voter numbers across nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by West Bengal with 83.86 lakh.  The revision identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters for removal. The consolidated electoral rolls across these regions saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.
